title: BatchCraft Advisor: interactive batching & cache recommendation cards with snapshot diff explorer and transactional rollback ledger
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a cohesive Console experience that surfaces automated batching and KV-cache recommendations as compact, actionable cards (BatchCraft Advisor). Each card must include a simulated snapshot diff that shows estimated cost delta, median P95 latency delta, and correctness risk score. Users must be able to stage multiple recommendations, run a dry-run simulation across a chosen time window, and apply changes transactionally with canary targets and single-click rollback. The feature will tie into Optimize's existing suggestion engine, runtime config APIs, and the audit ledger so every apply is recorded with a snapshot of before/after config and the evaluation dataset used for the simulation.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards render correctly in Console Optimize panel with title, summary metrics (estimated monthly $ change, est P95 latency change, risk score), and contextual reason (why recommendation was suggested)
Snapshot diff explorer shows side-by-side pre/post token-level simulation for a user-selected 24h/7d/30d window and allows toggling caching/batching knobs to recompute deltas client-side
Stage-and-apply flow supports batching of up to 10 independent recommendations into a single transactional change with canary rollout options (1%, 10%, 100%)
Apply operation creates an immutable audit ledger entry containing: author, timestamp, changed keys, prior config snapshot, post config snapshot, simulation inputs, and link to the simulation report
Rollback button is available on each ledger entry and can revert the exact applied change within the same release if used within 72 hours; rollback also produces its own ledger entry

All actions have corresponding Analytics events (optimize.card.view, optimize.card.stage, optimize.apply.start, optimize.apply.complete, optimize.rollback) and appear in per-customer cost and latency dashboards
E2E tests cover UI flows, API contract with runtime, dry-run accuracy tolerances (simulated cost within ±10% vs actual), and RBAC gating for apply/rollback actions
notes: Trade-offs: client-side re-simulations will be limited to aggregated heuristics for performance; full fidelity server re-sim will be offered as an optional background task
Design asked for compact cards to avoid workspace clutter; chosen pattern is a stacked card list with expand-to-inspector to view simulation details
We will reuse existing Optimize suggestion vectors and augment them with a short rationale sentence to improve trust
Backend needs a new transactional apply endpoint that writes both runtime config and ledger atomically; ENG-2419 owns the API design
Risk scoring combines cache-hit probability, model sensitivity, and historical quality regressions from evals service
qa_cases: Apply single cache TTL reduce recommendation in dry-run and verify no runtime change; compare simulated cost to historical cost delta
Stage 5 recommendations, run 10% canary, validate telemetry shows expected token rates and heartbeat metrics, then complete to 100%
Trigger rollback from ledger and confirm configs restored exactly and rollback ledger entry created
Verify RBAC: user without 'optimize.apply' cannot see Apply button but can view simulation
Edge case: conflicting recommendations touching same config key should surface merge preview and require explicit confirmation
metrics: Target: 12% average unit-cost reduction for workloads that accept batching/caching recommendations within 90 days
Adoption: 20% of eligible accounts use BatchCraft cards in first 6 weeks
Safety: <1% of applies require manual rollback after 30 days
Accuracy: simulation cost estimate within ±10% of observed cost after rolling to 100%
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dogfood in Redwood tenant with engineer + PM testers (2 weeks)
Phase 1: opt-in beta for power customers (10 customers, 4 weeks) with account-level feature flag
Phase 2: gradual enablement by default for accounts with low-sensitivity workloads (25% of customers per week)
risk_mitigation: Dry-run only mode by default; Apply requires explicit user confirmation and a typed acknowledgement for high-risk (>0.5) recommendations
Canary rollouts with automatic rollback triggers based on latency/cost/regression alerts
Immutable ledger and snapshot storage for forensic analysis; exports to S3 for long-term retention
RBAC gating to restrict apply/rollback to admins or ops roles
Provide 'undo' window (72 hours) for rapid reverts and automated quality-monitoring to catch regressions
